messages.content: I got an airline schedule-change email for Tucson. Can you sanity-check it before I accept anything? I mainly care about not wrecking Thursday night or Friday's hike.

Yes. The Tampa departure moved from 3:25 to 4:10 p.m. The DFW connection is now 52 minutes instead of 1 hour 37. It is legal, and the gates are projected in the same terminal, but it is not forgiving. Tucson arrival is still 8:58 p.m. The rental reservation is active; I added the flight number, and the counter says they hold delayed arrivals until 11:30 p.m.
So would you keep it or move us? I don't want a heroic connection with hiking packs.

Practical read: keep it unless the earlier flight is worth $186 total to you. Earlier option leaves Tampa at 1:05 p.m., has a 2-hour DFW buffer, and arrives 8:40 p.m. Same final evening, just less connection stress. The shifted itinerary is cheaper, no-change, and still workable if you go straight to the next gate.
Keep the shifted one then. What did the resort reconfirm?

Queen room is confirmed, with in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge. Pool is open 7 a.m.-10 p.m., hot tub 4-10 p.m., and fitness room is 24 hours. The spa hydro area is closed Friday morning for maintenance, but that is separate from the pool and hot tub.
Fine. Friday morning is hiking, not spa. Can you fix the return seats at all?
Good news: row 19 opened on the Monday return. I can move you from aisle-middle to 19A/19B, window-middle together, no extra charge. Outbound is still 16A/16B together.
Do that. And give me the Thursday and Monday sequence.

Done: return seats are now 19A/19B. Thursday plan is land, bags, rental counter, resort, and no grocery stop unless you land early; use packed snacks and get trail supplies Friday after breakfast. Monday: standard checkout works; leave the resort by 9:50 a.m., return the car by 11:00, and you have buffer for the 12:35 p.m. flight. Watch item is the DFW connection: if Tampa slips more than 25 minutes, ask the gate agent about Tucson protection before boarding.

messages.content: Back to work travel. Raleigh wants me for a pediatric handling seminar in late January, Saturday and Sunday. I need to be there Friday for a 5 p.m. lab setup window, and Sunday ends around 4:15, so I am assuming Monday home is smarter.

Got it. I will compare Friday outbound and Monday return as the base plan. For the hotel, should I lean toward campus walking distance, or toward a more predictable room setup even if it means a short drive?

Practical over cheapest. One stop is okay only if it doesn't put setup at risk. For the hotel, dependable room basics matter more than looking cute. Queen is fine, but I want coffee and a fridge confirmed if possible, and I do not want a borderline review situation before teaching days.

First pass for Jan 24-27, grouped by usefulness: 1. Best practical outbound: nonstop TPA-RDU 11:18 a.m.-1:04 p.m., about $258. This gives time for lunch, hotel check-in, and getting to the lab before 4:30. 2. Cheapest outbound: one stop via Atlanta, 12:35-4:06, about $212. I would not lead with it because one delay makes the 5 p.m. setup tight. 3. Safest but long day: nonstop 7:20-9:05, about $286. Plenty of buffer, but you are just waiting around. For Monday, the cleanest return is the 1:55-3:43 p.m. nonstop. The 4:40-8:05 p.m. one-stop saves about $20 but makes Monday drag. Sunday night after a 4:15 course end looks too rushed unless teardown is unusually light.
That Atlanta one is too tight. Is the 11:18 nonstop reliable enough, or is morning safer because of January weather?

The 11:18 nonstop is the better balance. It avoids a connection, arrives early afternoon, and still leaves roughly 3 hours before setup. The 7:20 gives extra winter cushion, but it does not solve much unless Raleigh has a major weather issue, in which case both flights could be affected.
Okay. Show me the hotels.

Two realistic tracks: Campus-adjacent hotel: Stateview Campus Inn, about 5 minutes on foot from the rehab lab, $184/night, Google rating 3.8. Recent reviews are uneven: noise, housekeeping delays, and older rooms. Queen room is bookable, but the mini-fridge is listed as request only and the desk agent would not guarantee it. Coffee is listed in some rooms and in the lobby. Small fitness room, no pool, no hot tub. Suite property: Raleigh Midtown Suites, 10-12 minutes by car, $162/night, Google rating 4.4. Queen studio confirmed, coffee maker, mini-fridge, desk, fitness room, and indoor pool. No hot tub. Free parking and cancellable until two days before arrival. Trade-off is simple: campus wins location; suite wins room certainty and better reviews, but it makes a car more useful.
No hot tub is annoying but not fatal for this one. Unclear fridge before a teaching weekend bothers me more. Does the suite pool look usable or is it a decorative puddle?

Usable, not resort-style. It is an indoor lap-style pool, open 6 a.m.-10 p.m., with the fitness room next door. It is not a spa setup and there is no hot tub, but it is a better recovery option than the campus hotel, which only has the small fitness room.
Then suite unless the university gives some reason I absolutely need to be on campus. Would you rent a car?

If you choose the suite, yes, a compact rental is the practical move. Estimated all-in is about $142-$155 for Friday afternoon through Monday noon. Rideshares would probably cost a little less only if everything is smooth, but you would have hotel-to-lab trips, a grocery stop, and possibly bins or teaching materials. If you stay on campus, I would wait on the rental until we know parking and access.
Let's not book until the university answers the parking and lab questions. What exactly do we need from them?

I would ask them these before committing: Friday setup: can you access the lab from 4:30-6:15 p.m., and who has keys? Weekend entry: which doors are open Saturday and Sunday, and is there an after-hours contact? Parking: which faculty or visitor lot can you use Friday evening, Saturday, and Sunday, and do they provide a permit? Materials: can your course bins stay locked in the lab or an office overnight? Sunday teardown: how late can you stay after the 4:15 end time? Load-in: is there a cart, elevator access, and a loading zone near the lab?
Add whether they have a locked cabinet specifically. I do not want to haul handling props back to the hotel Saturday night.

Added: locked cabinet or lockable office for Saturday night storage, with who is responsible for opening it Sunday morning. I also added whether the faculty lot permit covers Sunday or if campus security needs the car plate in advance.
For the return, keep Monday afternoon at the top. I want to end Sunday, sleep, check out normally, eat something, and then fly.

Then the 1:55 p.m. nonstop stays ranked first. It gives you normal checkout, lunch, rental return around noon, and a reasonable arrival back in Tampa. The 4:40 one-stop is a fallback if the nonstop spikes, but it gets you home after 8 p.m. The 10:10 a.m. return is out because it defeats the whole Monday buffer.
Any big caveats before I tell them the dates work?

Plain caveats: do not book the campus hotel unless they confirm the fridge and you accept the weaker reviews; the suite hotel has no hot tub and needs a short drive; the compact rental only makes sense if the university confirms a usable lot or permit; and the 11:18 outbound is strong, but fare and seat availability can change while we wait.
Send the university questions and mark my tentative plan as the 11:18 nonstop out, Monday 1:55 return, suite hotel, and compact rental if parking works.

Sent to the university coordinator. No bookings made. Tentative Raleigh stack is Friday Jan 24 TPA-RDU 11:18 a.m.-1:04 p.m., Monday Jan 27 RDU-TPA 1:55-3:43 p.m., Raleigh Midtown Suites, and a compact rental if the faculty lot or permit is confirmed. I set a fare and hotel watch; if the nonstop climbs more than about $40 or the suite cancellation terms tighten, I will flag it before you commit.

messages.content: Raleigh replied. Lab access Friday is 4:30 to 6:15, weekend parking is in a faculty lot, and they have a locked cabinet for my bins between course days. Can you book the sensible plan if prices held?

Prices mostly held. Before I book: Friday nonstop TPA-RDU 11:18 a.m.-1:04 p.m. is $262. Monday nonstop RDU-TPA 1:55-3:43 p.m. is $238. Raleigh Midtown Suites is $162/night, cancellable until Jan 22 at 6 p.m., queen studio with coffee maker, mini-fridge, desk, fitness room, and indoor pool; no hot tub. Compact rental is $151 pay-later, pickup at RDU and return Monday noon. Caveats are the suite is a 10-12 minute drive, and you need to print the faculty lot permit they are sending.
Book it. No campus hotel. Window seat if available, but don't pay for extra legroom.
Seat map check: free windows on the outbound are 18F or 28A; free windows on the return are 16A or 21F. Extra-legroom windows are available, but I will skip those. Want 18F outbound and 16A return?
Yes. And make sure the hotel is the queen studio, not two doubles.
Flights are booked. Confirmation RDU-JAN-5839. Friday Jan 24 TPA-RDU 11:18 a.m.-1:04 p.m., seat 18F. Monday Jan 27 RDU-TPA 1:55-3:43 p.m., seat 16A. No seat upgrade fees.
Good. Book the suite with the cancellable terms.

Reserved Raleigh Midtown Suites, Jan 24-27, queen studio. Confirmation RDU-SUITE-7142. Cancellable without penalty until Jan 22 at 6 p.m. The room notes confirm coffee maker, mini-fridge, work desk, and queen bed. Property amenities confirmed: fitness room and indoor pool. Missing amenity: no hot tub.
Car next. Compact is fine, not economy. Add my flight number so the pickup doesn't get weird.

Booked compact rental, confirmation CAR-RDU-2904. Pay-later, $151 estimated all-in. Pickup Friday at 1:30 p.m. at RDU, return Monday by noon. I added the inbound flight number and noted faculty-lot campus use.
Does the Friday timing still give me enough room for a grocery stop before setup?

Yes if the flight is close to on time. Working sequence: land 1:04, rental by about 1:35, hotel check-in around 2:10, quick grocery stop 2:45, leave for campus 3:55-4:05, arrive before the 4:30 setup window. If the flight is more than 45 minutes late, skip groceries and go hotel-to-campus.
Send me the final list and the watch items plainly.

Booked Raleigh plan: flights RDU-JAN-5839, hotel RDU-SUITE-7142, compact car CAR-RDU-2904. Friday outbound is 11:18 a.m.-1:04 p.m., seat 18F. Monday return is 1:55-3:43 p.m., seat 16A. Hotel is a cancellable queen studio with coffee maker, mini-fridge, desk, fitness room, and indoor pool; no hot tub. Watch items: print the faculty lot permit, bring the university contact number for Friday lab access, skip the grocery stop if the inbound is delayed, return the car by noon Monday, and cancel or adjust the hotel before Jan 22 at 6 p.m. if the course changes.
